headline: US equity futures dip into Q3 open as the dollar holds near 14-month highs, the yen hits a fresh 40-year low, and Iran peace-talk uncertainty keeps oil and rates elevated ahead of ADP, ISM Manufacturing, and Fed Chair Warsh's Sintra remarks.
stance: Cautious tilt at the open. The prior cash close left the SPX at 7,499 — a strong Q2 finish — but overnight futures slipped as US-Iran diplomacy remained fragile and the dollar stayed bid. The key risk today is Warsh's tone at the ECB Forum in Sintra: markets are already pricing a near-65% chance of a September Fed rate hike, so any hawkish signal could push the 10-year yield above 4.44% and compress equity multiples that are already stretched (CAPE 41.7x). Breadth is constructive — 61% of SPX names trade above their 50-day moving average — but positioning in equities is deeply extended short by speculators, which is a contrarian cushion if data disappoints.

news.head: US-Iran Doha talks — fragile progress
news.body: Iran and Qatar are holding technical talks in Doha on implementing the US-Iran memorandum of understanding, but Iran's top negotiator reiterated that the Strait of Hormuz remains Tehran's 'greatest instrument of power' and that final-deal negotiations will not begin until MoU provisions are implemented.

news.head: Fed Chair Warsh speaks at ECB Forum, Sintra
news.body: Warsh participates in a panel with BoE Governor Bailey, ECB President Lagarde, and BoC Governor Macklem today — his remarks on the Fed's balance sheet and rate path are the session's highest-impact catalyst, with markets pricing ~65% odds of a September hike.

news.head: SpaceX joins Nasdaq-100 on July 7
news.body: Nasdaq confirmed SpaceX (SPCX) will be added to the Nasdaq-100 index before the open on July 7, bypassing normal seasoning requirements; index-tracking funds must buy shares after the close on July 6.

news.head: ADP private payrolls & ISM Manufacturing due today
news.body: ADP June employment change (8:15 am ET, consensus ~120K vs 122K prior) and ISM Manufacturing PMI (10:00 am ET, consensus 53.9 vs 54.0 prior) are the two data events that will shape the market's Fed-hike narrative ahead of Friday's nonfarm payrolls.

news.head: Yen hits 40-year low
news.body: USD/JPY struck a fresh four-decade high above 162.80 in Asian trading overnight — Japan's top FX official acknowledged prior intervention was 'successful' but stopped short of threatening fresh action, keeping intervention risk elevated.

news.head: Gold drops under $4,000 in Asia
news.body: Gold traded around $3,983 overnight, under pressure for a third straight session as a firm dollar and rising Fed-hike expectations weigh on the non-yielding metal; bullion was on track for its worst quarterly performance since Q2 2013.

news.head: Eurozone CPI eases; ECB July hike now unlikely
news.body: Eurozone flash June CPI (expected 3.0% YoY vs 3.2% prior) follows softer prints from France, Germany, and Italy, making an ECB rate hike in July look very unlikely, per ECB policymaker commentary.

implications: Warsh's Sintra remarks are the day's swing factor: a hawkish lean on balance-sheet reduction or rate trajectory would lift the dollar, push yields higher, and amplify the overnight equity weakness.
ISM Manufacturing consensus of 53.9 is just below the prior 54.0 — a beat would reinforce the hawkish Fed narrative; a miss opens room for a relief rally in bonds and rate-sensitive equities.
ADP near 120K (consensus) should be a non-event for markets; an upside shock above ~150K would cement September hike bets.
The SpaceX (SPCX) Nasdaq-100 inclusion on July 7 means passive index funds must accumulate shares between now and the July 6 close — a structural demand tailwind for SPCX into next week.
USD/JPY above 162.80 is at a four-decade extreme; any Warsh comment that softens the dollar could trigger a sharp yen snap-back and unwind carry trades, which would pressure equities broadly.

Positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Nasdaq 100 futures (1st percentile of 3 years) and Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile) — a contrarian floor that limits the depth of a sell-off. However, speculators are heavily positioned long Copper futures (95th percentile of 3 years) — a contrarian warning for industrial metals.

watch.head: Warsh at Sintra (~10–11 am ET)
watch.body: Any signal on the pace of Fed balance-sheet reduction or explicit September hike guidance is the single biggest market-moving risk of the session.

watch.head: ISM Manufacturing 10:00 am ET
watch.body: A read above 54 reinforces the hawkish macro backdrop; below 53 would be the first clean catalyst for a bond-market rally and equity relief.

watch.head: USD/JPY intervention watch
watch.body: The pair traded above 162.80 overnight — a level well beyond the 160 threshold that triggered prior Ministry of Finance intervention; a sudden reversal would signal official action and could whipsaw risk assets.

watch.head: WTI crude & Iran headlines
watch.body: Oil is hovering near its prior cash close of $70.03/bbl; any breakdown in Doha talks or Strait of Hormuz incident would spike crude and force markets to re-price the Fed's inflation path higher.

watch.head: Nonfarm Payrolls (Thu Jul 2)
watch.body: The week's heavyweight data point arrives Thursday — consensus is for a strong print; a beat likely seals a September hike, making today's ADP a directional preview.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: PRIOR CASH CLOSE: 10-year Treasury yield 4.44%, 2-year yield 4.14%, yield curve (2s10s) +30 bps — positively sloped for the first time since 2022, signaling reduced near-term recession risk.

PRIOR CASH CLOSE: Real 10-year yield (after stripping out inflation expectations) stands at 2.2% — historically tight territory that pressures asset valuations, particularly long-duration growth stocks.
PRIOR CASH CLOSE: 10-year inflation breakeven at 2.24% — markets expect inflation to run just above the Fed's 2% target, supporting the case for at least one hike.
Bond-market volatility (MOVE index) closed at 72 — calm by recent standards, suggesting bond traders are not yet panicking, but Warsh's remarks today could change that quickly.
PRIOR CASH CLOSE: DXY dollar index at 101.17, on track for a second straight monthly gain and its strongest June since 2025, driven by Fed hike pricing and a fiscally passive Bank of Japan.

OVERNIGHT: USD/JPY struck a fresh 40-year high above 162.80 in Asian hours — the yen is at its most extreme reading in the 3-year dataset (100th percentile), raising the risk of sudden official intervention.
Financial conditions remain loose: the Chicago Fed ANFCI reads -0.477 and the St. Louis FSI reads -0.96 — both well below zero, meaning money is still easy to borrow despite higher rates.
Today's calendar: ADP (8:15 am), ISM Manufacturing (10:00 am), EIA oil inventories (10:30 am), and Fed Chair Warsh at ECB Forum Sintra.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in 3-month SOFR interest-rate futures (1st percentile of 3 years, diverging sharply from hedgers) — a contrarian-bullish lean for short-term rates, implying the rate-hike fear may be overdone in the front end of the curve.

single_name.note: Matador Resources (oil & gas producer) — large off-exchange block buying (quiet institutional accumulation) and a burst of unusual options buying, company insiders have been buying (2 insider rules fired), trading above its 200-day moving average; shorts are heavy at 7.6 days-to-cover, raising squeeze risk if oil stabilizes around $70.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: PRIOR CASH CLOSE: S&P 500 at 7,499.36, Nasdaq 100 at 26,213.72, Dow at 52,319.20 — all three closed Q2 strongly, with the SPX up ~14% for the quarter and NDX up ~20%.
OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET: US equity index futures pointed lower at the Q3 open, with caution stemming from ongoing Iran uncertainty and anticipation of potentially hawkish Fed commentary from Sintra.

PRIOR CASH CLOSE: VIX (the stock market's 'fear gauge') at 16.45 — low and complacent; the equity-credit correlation at 0.757 means stocks and credit markets are moving closely together, so any credit wobble would quickly show up in equities.
PRIOR CASH CLOSE: Nasdaq volatility index (VXN) at 27.11 — elevated relative to VIX, reflecting lingering unease in high-growth tech names despite the Q2 recovery.
Market breadth is improving: 61% of SPX stocks and 61.5% trade above their 50-day and 200-day moving averages respectively — this is healthier than a market carried by a handful of mega-cap names.

PRIOR CASH CLOSE: Equity risk premium (the extra return stocks offer over risk-free bonds) is -2.08% — stocks are cheaper on a yield basis than Treasuries, a historically unusual and cautionary valuation signal at CAPE 41.7x.
SpaceX (SPCX) joins the Nasdaq-100 before the July 7 open — index funds must buy between now and July 6 close, creating a structural demand tailwind for SPCX this week.
The banking sector (BKX) relative to the SPX closed at 0.0914 — banks are holding their relative ground, a positive sign that financial stress is not building.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Nasdaq 100 futures (4th percentile of 3 years) and Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile, with hedgers positioned at the opposite extreme) — both are contrarian floors suggesting the next big move in small- and mid-caps could be to the upside. VIX futures are also at the 12th percentile of speculator net positioning — another contrarian-bullish lean for equities.

single_name.note: Six Flags Entertainment (theme park operator, Consumer Cyclical) — large off-exchange block buying and a burst of unusual options buying, company insiders have been buying; shorts are heavy at 9.2 days-to-cover, raising squeeze risk; trading above its 200-day moving average.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: PRIOR CASH CLOSE: High-yield credit spreads at 280 bps over investment-grade — elevated but not distressed; investment-grade option-adjusted spreads at 76 bps — both consistent with a functioning credit market.
PRIOR CASH CLOSE: The HY/IG ETF ratio at 1.3639 — junk bonds are holding up relative to safer corporate debt, suggesting credit investors are not yet fleeing risk.
Interbank funding stress is essentially zero: FRA-OIS and SOFR-OIS spreads are both at -1 bp — banks are borrowing freely from each other, no hidden plumbing stress.
Commercial paper funding cost (CPFF spread) is just 18 bps — corporations can raise short-term cash cheaply, another green light for liquidity.

PRIOR CASH CLOSE: Bank reserves at $2,951.4 billion and the Fed's overnight reverse repo (RRP) facility at $26.9 billion — reserves are ample and the RRP is nearly drained, meaning excess cash has moved into the real economy and private markets.
M2 money supply growing at 5.58% YoY — healthy nominal growth backdrop that supports nominal earnings, though it also feeds the inflation story the Fed is watching closely.
Bank credit expanding at 6.3% YoY and loan syndication rates at 6.92% — lending is growing but borrowing costs remain high, a squeeze on leveraged borrowers.

Treasury General Account (TGA) at $918.7 billion — the government's cash balance is large; any drawdown to fund spending would inject liquidity into the banking system, a net positive for market plumbing.
sections.positioning: Primary dealers hold high-yield bond inventory at the 89th percentile of their 3-year net-position range — dealers are heavily positioned in junk bonds, a contrarian warning that spread compression from here may be limited.

single_name.note: NewtekOne (small-business lender, Financial Services) — large off-exchange block buying and a burst of unusual options buying, company insiders have been buying (2 insider rules fired); shorts are exceptionally heavy at 17.7 days-to-cover, creating significant squeeze risk if the credit environment holds; trading above its 200-day moving average.
